guard_streams.source: Broadband and landline faults and problems
guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer troubleshooting and in-home factors do not establish network availability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: The consumer guide was published on 13 October 2023.
The guide was last updated on 8 April 2026.
Telephone extension leads and wiring changes can cause interference and lower speed.
Microfilters should be fitted to every used phone socket where required.
Electrical devices and wireless emitters can interfere with routers.
Ofcom advises placing a router on a table or shelf rather than the floor.
Building work and additional walls can reduce wireless performance.
Online or telephone purchases generally carry a 14-day cancellation period.
Customers receiving speeds far below estimates may be protected by the voluntary speed Code of Practice.
Providers may ask for a direct Ethernet test to help identify whether a line fault exists.

guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly market volumes and revenues are aggregate sector statistics and cannot verify selected-parcel serviceability or speed.

facts.detail: UK fixed-voice service revenues were £891.9 million in Q1 2026.
The number of fixed lines fell to 20.7 million.
Fixed-originated call volumes were 3.32 billion minutes.
There were 29.4 million fixed-broadband lines at the end of Q1 2026.
Fixed-broadband lines increased by 282,000 year on year.
Mobile telephony retail revenues were £3.57 billion.
Active mobile subscriptions excluding M2M totalled 90.6 million.
Dedicated mobile-broadband subscriptions reached 5.2 million.
Mobile data usage reached 3,042 petabytes.
Ofcom provides Q1 2026 market-data outputs in both PDF and CSV formats.

guard_streams.source: Social tariffs: Cheaper broadband and phone packages
guard_streams.write_limit: Tariff eligibility, prices and advertised speeds are affordability information; they do not establish physical coverage or measured parcel speed.

facts.detail: The social-tariff guide was published on 6 March 2024.
It was last updated on 22 June 2026.
Social tariffs target households receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit and some other benefits.
They are delivered like normal packages but at a lower price.
The listed current price range is £10 to £24 per month.
Most listed tariffs offer speeds above 30 Mbit/s.
Setup costs should be zero or small and disclosed before signup.
Customers can switch free of charge where their current provider offers a social tariff.
The agreed tariff price does not rise mid-contract.
Customers do not pay a fee to leave a social tariff before contract end.
